Yes. I’d attach it to the existing flight plan: Monday afternoon Delta nonstop ATL-ORD and Thursday afternoon ORD-ATL around 4 p.m. Book the closer hotel on the refundable, non-prepaid rate; note that the higher nightly rate is justified by the short walk to the Loop meeting center and avoids the suite hotel’s less predictable morning commute.
Please add a quiet-room request too, away from elevators if possible.
Added to the hotel request: quiet room, away from elevators and ice machine, high floor if available. It is not guaranteed, but it will be on the reservation.
What exactly should I write about breakfast? I don't want it to look like I forgot that piece.

Say: Breakfast is not included in the rate. Paid breakfast is available at or near the hotel, and there are quick coffee/breakfast options on the short walk toward the meeting center. That keeps it transparent without reopening the suite-hotel tradeoff.
And Monday dinner? I may reach the hotel right around normal dinner time.

Use the hotel restaurant first if it is serving; otherwise there should be easy Loop/River North casual options by short walk or quick rideshare. I would not reserve anything unless the flight shifts later.
Can you check seats before I finalize? I had no window on the outbound.
Outbound still has no standard window open. The Thursday return does have a standard window in the back half. Do you want me to take that and leave the outbound as-is for a check-in recheck?
Yes. Take the return window and book the hotel refundable.

Booked: the closer Chicago hotel on the refundable rate, with breakfast marked as not included and the quiet-room request attached. And first evening/Tuesday morning?

Check in, use the hotel restaurant or nearby Loop/River North casual dinner, then keep Tuesday simple: paid hotel breakfast or a quick coffee stop by 7:30 and walk to the 8:30 session. messages.content: Back from Chicago, and Denver is next. I’ve been assigned to a client configuration workshop Monday Dec 8 through Thursday Dec 11. Tuesday and Wednesday are full client days, Thursday is probably a debrief, but I don’t have the office address yet.

We can frame it, but I would not route an approval packet until the address lands. For now, build around ATL-DEN nonstops, a Monday arrival with winter-delay buffer, and a hotel in the right business district once we know whether the client is downtown or in the Tech Center area. Are you solo, and is there any Monday evening setup?
Solo. No answer on setup. I may need to be available Monday evening, but nobody has said I have to be onsite.

Then avoid a late arrival. The best flight windows to compare are a midday Atlanta departure that gets you to Denver mid-afternoon, or a mid-afternoon departure that gets you there around dinner. I would keep connections out of the first pass; December is not the time to add a Midwest layover just to save a little.
If setup becomes real, should I push earlier?

Yes. If they need Monday setup, take the midday nonstop so a delay does not wipe out the evening. If Monday is just travel and email availability, the mid-afternoon nonstop is probably fine and preserves more of your morning in Atlanta.
What about Thursday coming home? I don't know when the debrief ends.

Hold two return choices for now: a late-afternoon nonstop if the debrief ends by noon or 1, and an evening nonstop as backup if they run long. Once the debrief time is confirmed, choose the earliest one that does not create a client-site-to-DEN scramble.
Delta if reasonable, but don't force it.

Agreed. Start with Delta because the ATL schedules are usually strong, then compare United and Southwest for timing or fare policy. For this trip, nonstop and a workable return buffer matter more than the carrier name.
Can you lay out the hotel areas? I keep hearing either downtown or Tech Center.

If the office is downtown or near the convention/financial district, choose Downtown/LoDo: better restaurants, easier no-car evenings, and a short rideshare or walk to many offices. If it is Denver Tech Center or Greenwood Village, stay there instead: less interesting at night, but much better for early client mornings and usually easier parking. I’d avoid an airport hotel unless the client is actually near DIA.
Would you rent a car?

Not until the address is known. Downtown points to no rental car: rail or rideshare should work. DTC is a maybe: rent if the office is on a suburban campus, parking is easy, or team dinners are spread out; skip it if the hotel is close and rideshares are reliable. Snow and parking fees are reasons to keep it optional.
Give me the client questions so I can send one clean email.

Ask for the exact office address; whether Monday evening setup is required and where; expected Thursday debrief end time; any recommended hotel block or preferred area; parking/security check-in instructions; and whether there are team dinners. After that, route a refundable plan: ATL-DEN nonstop Monday, DEN-ATL Thursday late afternoon or evening, and a strong guest-rated business hotel in the correct area with a practical breakfast and dinner plan.
